# comprehensions

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/lowering/comprehensions"
```

Package comprehensions lowers collection expressions into Go ranges and stores.

A comprehension produces a slice or map by evaluating its generators and adding their outputs. This rule owns collection construction, range selection, and output insertion. A slice with one output on every visit can allocate once when the checked source permits an exact count. Other forms append as their outputs run. Hidden builtin names use the existing shared import operations.

Shared operations retain checked element and key types, give generator bindings fresh names, and evaluate output operands in source order. Their ordinary range and jump handling keeps filters, nested ranges, returns, and continues at the source execution point. Collection output state belongs to the current function context; nested functions do not inherit that state.

Output expressions can contain other TGo rules. The supplied context returns to the dispatcher for those expressions. This keeps collection decisions separate from error and branch rules without changing their execution order.

## func Expression

```go
func Expression(r *shared.Context, call *ast.CallExpr, record *frontend.Comprehension) shared.Result
```

Expression constructs a collection at its source evaluation point.

## func Output


Output evaluates output operands and inserts them into the collection.
